sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid pages yamp1243 (Yamphe, bookkeeping), sout2734 (Southern Yamphu), yamp1242 (Yamphu): reference lists
sources.note: Southern Yamphu has 8 refs, none grammar/phonology/sketch (surveys, wordlists, Hansson 1991, atlases, ISO CR); Yamphu has Rutgers 1998 as sole grammar.

sources.citation: Hilty, Holly J. & Jessica R. Mitchell. 2014. Yamphu: A Sociolinguistic Survey. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2014-007 (= Linguistic Survey of Nepal report, 2012). 193 pp.
sources.note: Nothing: no occurrence of stress/accent/tone in the text; sec. 2.4.2 defers to Rutgers 1998 for linguistics; Appendix C wordlists (Hedangna, Devitar, Rajarani, Pangma) carry no stress marks. Sec. 6.1 explains 'Yamphe' is Hansson's term used by no speaker; Devitar (Matsyapokhari VDC) and Rajarani/Bodhe (Dhankuta) = Southern Yamphu [lrr].

sources.citation: Rai, Tara Bir. 2012. Yamphu and English Pronominals. M.Ed. thesis, Tribhuvan University (on the 'Yubhali dialect' of Matsyapokhari/Barabise VDCs, i.e. the Devitar-area variety now coded Southern Yamphu).
sources.note: p. 9: Yamphu dialects differ 'in phonology, vocabulary and supra-segmental features level viz. tone, juncture, stress etc.' -- no rule for stress placement; Appendix D gives vowel/consonant charts only. Also states the Hedangna-Num dialect is spoken in Pathibhara and Num VDCs.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2011. Change Request Number 2011-152: merge Yamphe [yma] into Southern Lorung [lrr], rename Southern Yamphu (effective 2012-02-03). SIL International.
sources.note: Nothing; identity document only (lexical similarity Yamphe-S.Lorung 83-86%, RTT scores; both groups self-identify as 'Yamphu').

sources.citation: Gerber, Pascal. 2023. Vergleich und Rekonstruktion der Oberarun-Sprachen (Kiranti): Mit einer Skizze des Westmewahang. PhD dissertation, Universität Bern, xxvii+905 pp.

sources.note: Comparative phonology/reconstruction of all Upper Arun varieties (Yamphu, Lohorung, Mewahang); the likeliest place for any statement covering Southern Yamphu (Devitar/Rajarani) prosody and for a cross-variety accent statement.

sources.citation: van Driem, George. 2001. Languages of the Himalayas, vol. 2 (Kiranti section on Yamphu, 'Yamphe', Lohorung). Leiden: Brill.

sources.note: Discusses the Yamphu/Yamphe/Yakkhaba naming tangle (cited p. 623 by Hilty & Mitchell) and may summarise Upper Arun phonology incl. accent second-hand.

sources.citation: Rutgers, Roland. 1998. Yamphu: Grammar, Texts & Lexicon. (Languages of the Greater Himalayan Region 2.) Leiden: Research School CNWS. ISBN 90-5789-012-7.

sources.note: Only full grammar in the Yamphu cluster, with a phonology chapter that almost certainly states stress/accent; describes the northern (Hedangna) variety = yamp1242, which is what Hansson's original 'Yamphe' denoted; nearest first-hand statement obtainable for this languoid.
